text: This video runs one strategy in eight stacks.
doeff runs Python functions that yield effects to handlers.
We read each new layer, from a risk stop to a test.
Every stack here runs the same sma_cross.
risk first passes each Order on to the exchange.
On a buy, it notes the entry price.
If one trade lost over 2.0, it returns a sentence.
Otherwise it resumes that k with the price.
The fourth Order, a sell at t=66, lost 2.51.
risk drops that k, and the strategy ends there.
sweep spawns one backtest for each pair of averages.
Then it gathers the six results and sorts them.
scheduled runs the six tasks side by side.
recording passes Tick and Order on, and keeps each answer.
replaying answers each one from the tape instead.
317 answers replay the session: pnl 50.79 again.
live awaits the exchange client for each Tick.
For each Order, it awaits the client to place it.
await_handler runs those awaits on an asyncio loop.
The same strategy trades live: pnl 6.96.
A test is one more stack, on the virtual clock.
first_trade asks the time and returns it with the line.
It drops k, so the run ends at the first trade: 21 minutes.
Eight stacks, one strategy, nothing patched.
